subject: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Finex streaming + concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexcapital.com>, Grace Lee <grace.lee@finexcapital.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap  throughput / latency targets (Finex)

Hi Samir / Grace  great call earlier. Quick recap and next steps on sizing so we can lock in a proposal: 

1) Workload profile (what you confirmed):
- Primary flow: document ingestion -> extract/summarize -> realtime QA (streaming responses to user UI).
- Average prompt length (incl. system + user): ~350 tokens.
- Typical response length: 220 tokens.
- Concurrency: steady-state 80 concurrent users; peak burst up to 420 concurrent users during market hours.
- Latency target (95th): 400ms for streaming-first UX; non-streaming SLO (completion): 900ms.
- Expected sustained QPS (requests/sec): steady 55 QPS, peak ~290 QPS for burst windows.

2) Questions we left on the call:
- Do peaks correspond to ~10-15 minute windows or longer sustained spikes?
- Any hard SLA for token-level billing windows or throttling?
- Are there any long-tail conversation sessions (>= 20 turns) we should account for?

3) Next steps (to-do):
- Samir / Grace: share 1 week of anonymized request logs (timestamps, tokens in, tokens out, session id) or a small sample export so we can run a tokens/sec profile.
- Redwood: we will run throughput modeling (tokens/sec, GPU pool sizing) and share a recommended Dedicated configuration + fallback hosted variant. I attached a quick spreadsheet with QPS -> GPU estimates.
- Schedule: aim to have the sizing deck and cost estimate by EOD Friday PST.

Attachments: finex_qps_spreadsheet.xlsx (sizing workbook stub)

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexcapital.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace Lee <grace.lee@finexcapital.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap  throughput / latency targets (Finex)

Thanks Rafael  quick clarifications: 
- Peak windows are typically short: 812 minutes around market opens and earnings releases, but we also have longer midday spikes (20145 minutes) during big news.
- For session length: ~92% are under 6 turns, ~6% are 6120 turns, ~2% >20 turns. The long-tail sessions mostly come from analyst teams.
- Regarding tokens: the 220 token average response is accurate; we occasionally have longer completions for deep-dive Q&A (up to ~600 tokens).

I'll work on exporting a 2472 hour sample this afternoon and will drop in Drive. Grace  looping you to confirm if we can include headers (no PII) and session IDs.

Samir
Senior Product Manager, Finex Capital
samir.shah@finexcapital.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finexcapital.com>, Grace Lee <grace.lee@finexcapital.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap  throughput / latency targets (Finex)

Perfect  that's helpful context. A few notes based on what you shared: 

- For streaming-first UX with 95th=400ms, we'll recommend a combination of low-latency model variants (quantized small-medium footprints) and a dedicated GPU pool sized to absorb 80 steady concurrent sessions and headroom for 400+ burst concurrency.
- Tokens/sec modeling: using your averages (prompt 350 + response 220 = 570 tokens per request), steady 55 QPS -> ~31,350 tokens/sec sustained; peak 290 QPS -> ~165,300 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency mapping: if UI streams partial tokens early, effective perceived latency improves but backend must sustain token emission rates. For 400 concurrent streaming sessions emitting avg 20 tokens/sec per session, that's 8,000 tokens/sec just for active streaming  will factor into the GPU scheduling.

Action items for sizing calc:
- Neha: can you run the spreadsheet with these token/sec numbers and try 1) conservative packing (no KV cache reuse) and 2) aggressive caching/batching numbers?
- We'll include fallback hosted endpoints for elasticity during >95th percentile bursts.

I'll attach a short architecture diagram (finex_arch_diagram.png) to show where caching lives (edge vs model cache).

Rafael

From: Grace Lee <grace.lee@finexcapital.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap  throughput / latency targets (Finex)

Thanks  the token/sec calc looks reasonable. A couple of asks before we sign off on a sizing recommendation: 

1) Can you provide an explicit SLA statement we can take to procurement? We need: 95th latency SLO (streaming) = 400ms, target uptime 99.9% (monthly), and failover behavior if dedicated capacity is saturated (automatic fallback to hosted with degraded latency cap).
2) Cost estimate: we need a 12-month committed estimate for Dedicated (monthly committed GPUs) + a per-token surcharge for hosted fallback. If you can give a ballpark range now, we can prep Finance.

I'll drop the sample logs in Drive (link will follow)  confirmed we can include session IDs + timestamps (no PII).

Grace
Director, Platform Product, Finex Capital

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Lee <grace.lee@finexcapital.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap  throughput / latency targets (Finex)

Grace  thanks. We'll prepare: 
- A one-page SLA statement (95th streaming latency 400ms; completion 95th 900ms; 99.9% uptime target) and clear failover behavior.
- A 12-month Dedicated capacity estimate with a hosted-fallback per-token surcharge range.
- Neha will share two GPU configuration options (conservative vs optimized with batching/caching) and expected tokens/sec capacity per pool.

Target: deliver the sizing deck + preliminary pricing by EOD Friday PST (as Rafael noted). If the Drive link hits us, we'll ingest the sample and run the exact tokens/sec profile.

Regards,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
